Isotropic 2 mm spatial smoothness calibration, 05 Oct 2026

Scope: SUSAN with an automask for brightness-threshold estimation and no
previous input mask, an fMRIPrep input mask, or a TemplateFlow input mask;
Gaussian AFNI 3dBlurInMask and 3dmerge with no previous input mask.
Kernels measured separately: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 mm FWHM.
Tools: FSL 6.0.7.16 and AFNI 26.0.00.

The experiment includes one run per subject: 12 subjects from three internal
fMRIPrep cohorts, resampled with AFNI cubic interpolation to isotropic 2 mm,
and 10 independent subjects with fMRIPrep 25.2.5 res-2 outputs. Six internal
subjects (two per cohort) supply 36 calibration observations per condition.
The remaining six internal subjects and all 10 external subjects supply 96
held-out observations per condition. External subjects are never used to fit
coefficients or establish error limits. Internal resampling broadens baseline
smoothness coverage but does not replace evidence from genuine res-2 outputs.

SUSAN uses the production full-run brightness threshold, temporal mean image,
and temporal-minimum extents, then smooths the 96 distributed volumes used by
the estimator. A full-run replay confirms this operator agrees with production
spatial_smooth(). Gaussian smoothing acts independently on each volume.
Smoothness measurement uses classic FWHM after cubic detrending, demeaning,
and voxelwise MAD scaling. Input masks and automasks match postprocessing.
Sampled NIfTI images are reconstructed with spatial header geometry to avoid
stale AFNI extensions that describe the original time dimension.

The original coefficients are evaluated first. Separate 2 mm fits retain the
two-parameter quadrature model:
  effective_kernel = b0 * requested_kernel_mm + b1 * voxel_mm
  expected_post_fwhm = sqrt(pre_fwhm^2 + effective_kernel^2)
Fit by minimizing post-FWHM squared error on the calibration observations,
with b0 > 0 and effective_kernel(3 mm) > 0. Positivity and monotonicity therefore
hold throughout 3--8 mm. Coarser-resolution coefficients remain unchanged.

Leave-one-internal-cohort-out checks fit the four calibration subjects from
two cohorts and evaluate all four subjects in the excluded cohort, producing
72 observations per condition. The 2 mm error limit is the larger of the
original condition's limit and the maximum error on the 36 excluded calibration
observations in those cohort-transfer folds, rounded up
to 0.1 mm, capped at 1.0 mm. Held-out subjects do not determine the limit. This error-limit rule was specified before the
final template-mask measurements completed, after initial transfer errors
exceeded the original limits. It is an empirical acceptance limit, not a
statistical confidence bound. Promotion requires every held-out error and
every cohort-transfer error to meet that limit. Aggregate coefficients and
errors are in spatial_smooth_calibration_2mm.csv.

Support is restricted to all three voxel spacings equal to 2 mm within 1e-6
and kernels within 3--8 mm. Anisotropic grids with geometric mean 2 mm are
excluded. Untested estimator preparation, Gaussian input-mask conditions,
and SUSAN without a threshold-estimation mask are excluded. Continuous kernel
support between measured integer kernels assumes the fitted monotone model.
Validation also requires a measurable post-smoothing FWHM increase, so an
unchanged image cannot pass solely because of the acceptance limit.

Independent production replays check full-run outputs and deliberately wrong
kernel controls. All serialized evidence consists of scalar summaries and
small geometry metadata. NIfTI images remain separate scratch files; voxel
arrays and image objects never enter calibration JSON or provenance.
